pages.profileIntro: Who you are, how customers reach you when something happens, and what you deliver. A customer weighs the rest of your answers by this.

marketing.title: One security questionnaire for <blue>all your customers</blue>.
marketing.subtitle: Your customers fall under NIS 2 and have to check how securely their suppliers work. So they send you security questionnaires, each one in a different format. Here you answer the questions once and release them to every customer who invites you. <os>Open Source</os>, no lock-in.
marketing.entityDoor: Does your own company fall under NIS 2? Check applicability.
marketing.regLine: NIS 2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555 · CIR 2024/2690 · ENISA TIG v1.0
marketing.screenshotAlt: The nisd2.eu supplier portal with a completed questionnaire
marketing.step1Body: Sign in, enter your company name and domain. The profile belongs to you, not to one of your customers.
marketing.step2Body: Up to {count} questions on commitments, security management, incident plans and access; you only see the ones that fit what you deliver. Every question names the provision it rests on. Drafts are saved as you go.
marketing.step3Body: Each customer gets their own private link. They see your profile, the systems you run for them, and your certificates. They do not need an account.
marketing.step4Body: If a customer's system is affected, you report it from inside the portal. Only that one customer sees the report. It helps them with their duty under Art. 21(2)(d) NIS2 to keep the security of their supply chain in view.
marketing.coversIntro: The questions rest on Art. 21 NIS2, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 and ENISA's Technical Implementation Guidance v1.0 from June 2025; each names the provision it rests on and, where one applies, the matching ISO 27001 control. It asks what a customer needs for their supply chain, and no more. The question set is public on GitHub.
marketing.covers1Body: Legal name, address, domain, and who a customer reaches when something goes wrong. Plus the window you commit to responding in.
marketing.covers2Body: How your company runs information security: management system, certification, training, vulnerability handling, access, continuity planning.
marketing.covers3Body: Right to audit, data processing agreement, subcontractors, confidentiality, hand-back at the end of the contract, notification of material changes.
marketing.covers4Body: Whether you hold your customers' data, reach their systems, enter their premises or deliver software. A tax adviser, a cleaning company and a software house each see only the questions that fit them.
marketing.covers5Body: Upload ISO 27001, BSI C5, TISAX, SOC 2 or an equivalent as a PDF. Customers see how long it stays valid.
marketing.privacyBody: There is no public supplier directory. Only the customers you release it to can see your profile, and each of them can end their own access. No public address, no search engine indexing.
marketing.bsiQuote: Wir begrüßen aktuelle Vorstöße der Wirtschaft, einen einheitlichen Fragenkatalog für Lieferanten zu erarbeiten.
marketing.bsiQuoteTranslation: We welcome current industry initiatives to develop a unified question set for suppliers.
marketing.bsiAttribution: BSI, FAQ on NIS 2 (supply chains and security). This portal is exactly that: a unified question set, built by a company, free for anyone to use.
marketing.whyFree: The supplier portal costs nothing and the code is open. We earn from the guided walkthrough for companies under NIS 2, not from your data. Platform and question set are on GitHub, so you can check for yourself.
marketing.footerBody: Sign in, enter your company name and domain, work through the questionnaire at your own pace. When you are ready, invite your customers.
marketing.metaTitle: NIS 2 supplier portal: one security questionnaire for all customers
marketing.metaDescription: Answer your customers' NIS 2 questions once and release the answers to every customer who invites you. Structured to ENISA TIG v1.0 and CIR 2024/2690. Open Source, no lock-in.

identity.title: Who you are
identity.why: So a customer can list you unambiguously among their suppliers.

contacts.title: How to reach you when something happens
contacts.why: A customer needs a contact point for security matters for each direct supplier.

delivery.title: What you deliver and what you reach
delivery.why: Whether you hold your customers' data, reach their systems or enter their premises decides which questions you see next and how much your answers weigh for a customer.

commitments.title: What you commit to customers
commitments.why: Where appropriate, these points belong in your contract with a customer. Here you say up front what you are prepared to do.

operations.title: How you run security
operations.why: Customers also choose suppliers by their security practices. A certificate that covers your service already tells them much of this.

access.title: How you access customers
access.why: Signing in to a customer's systems or entering their premises carries responsibility for their security. Here you say how you secure that access.

saas.title: Software as a service (SaaS)
saas.why: Whether customers can protect their accounts with a second factor, and how fast your service runs again after an outage.

onPrem.title: Software on the customer's premises
onPrem.why: How long you supply security updates for your software, and how a customer can tell that it and its updates can be trusted.

customerView.revokedBody: You will no longer receive notifications from this supplier.
customerView.servicesTitle: Systems this supplier runs for you
customerView.servicesIntro: These answers apply to your relationship only. Other customers of the same supplier see their own systems, not these.
customerView.servicesEmpty: No system has been recorded for you yet.
customerView.nothingDeclared: No details have been provided for this system yet.
customerView.incidentsIntro: Only incidents this supplier reported to you. Keeping track of them is part of Article 21(2)(d) NIS2.
customerView.incidentsEmpty: No incident has been reported to you so far.

assets.empty: No assets recorded for this customer yet. Use Add asset to record the first one.

incidents.intro: Notify {recipient} about a security incident that affects the assets you manage for them. It helps the customer with their duty under Art. 21(2)(d) NIS2 to keep the security of their supply chain in view.
incidents.managerIntro: Notify one customer about a security incident that affects the assets you manage for them. Each notice goes to exactly one customer. It helps the customer with their duty under Art. 21(2)(d) NIS2 to keep the security of their supply chain in view.
incidents.noCustomers: You need at least one active customer before you can report an incident. <link>Add a customer</link>
incidents.affectedAssets: Affected assets (optional, leave blank for a general notice)
incidents.noAssets: No assets recorded for this customer yet. The notice goes out without naming an asset.
incidents.noAssetsHint: You add assets on the customer's page.
incidents.descriptionPlaceholder: Between 14:00 and 15:30 UTC the customer portal was unreachable…
incidents.descriptionHint: Do not include internal investigation notes or personal data. The customer reads the text exactly as you write it. The email they get does not contain it, it links to your notice.

access.revokeConfirm: End access for this customer? They will no longer be able to see your security profile.
access.clausesIntro: What you have agreed with this customer in your contract. Based on point 5.1.4 of the Annex to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 and ENISA's Technical Implementation Guidance on it.
